old: Its name may trace back to a Burmese port once known for shipping spices across the sea.
Before it meant a sweet paste, the word may have simply meant 'spice box' in Arabic.
Italian speakers shaped the word further, possibly under the influence of pane, their word for bread.
clues: This sweet confection's name is believed to trace back to an Arabic word for a spice box, itself named after a Burmese port famous for exporting spices.
A pliable paste of ground almonds and sugar, unlike all-sugar fondant, often molded into tiny fruits and animals. Its final form was likely shaped by an Italian word for bread.
Bakers roll it over a traditional British Christmas cake beneath the white icing, and it hides as a sweet seam in the center of German stollen.
